---
id: SA-0370
title: _export_from_volume's already-read head sha dies with a patch.json write that fails after patch.diff already landed
type: bug
priority: 2
estimated_lines: 110
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - saffron/cell/session.py
  - tests/test_session.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - harness/**
  - images/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/cell/runtime.py
  - saffron/cell/runtimes/**
  - saffron/cell/worktree.py
  - saffron/cell/proxy.py
  - saffron/events.py
  - saffron/ledger.py
  - saffron/record/**
  - saffron/gates/**
  - saffron/phases/**
  - saffron/repos/**
  - saffron/task.py
  - saffron/cli.py
  - saffron/batch.py
  - saffron/view/**
  - tests/conftest.py
  - tests/test_events.py
  - tests/test_runtime.py
  - tests/test_scheduler.py
  - tests/test_queued_specs.py
  - tests/test_worktree.py
  - tests/fixtures/**
budget_usd: 20
max_attempts: 3
max_turns: 60
risk: standard
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      In `_export_from_volume`, `worktree.head_sha(target)` answers before
      either file is written. At base (`saffron/cell/session.py:1004-1009`)
      that answer is held under the local name `read_sha`. It is copied
      into the function's own `head_sha` only on the line directly after
      `patch.diff` and `patch.json` are both written (`:1009`). The outer
      `head_sha` is the name both the `try`'s own `return` and the `except
      Exception as exc:` beneath it (`:1017-1023`) hand back. So an
      exception raised between that read answering and that copy running
      reaches the `except` with `head_sha` still the `None` it was
      initialised to (`:975`). That exception can come from the
      changed-files read right after the sha (`:1005`), or from the
      `patch.json` write itself (`:1008`), including after `patch.diff` was
      already written to `task_dir` at `:1007`. Either way the function
      returns `None` though a real sha was already known, and though a
      real, readable `patch.diff` sits in `task_dir` under no identity the
      caller can find it by. The cell path this function stands in for does
      not have this gap. It binds its own `head_sha` the line directly
      after its own read (`saffron/cell/session.py:1098`), before either of
      its own writes (`:1099-1105`). So the identical failure there, a
      `worktree.changed_files` call raising while `patch.json` is built,
      still returns the sha already known. `_export_from_volume` is
      changed to bind `head_sha` the same way, the instant
      `worktree.head_sha(target)` answers and not after the writes that may
      still fail. No other line in `_export_from_volume` changes. The two
      inner `try` blocks around the subject read and the patch read, the
      `no_commits` return, the `exported` and `export_failed` teardown
      lines, and the outer `finally`'s network removal all stay exactly as
      they read at base. The witness drives both failure points on the
      same volume: the changed-files read failing before any write, and
      the `patch.json` write failing after `patch.diff` already landed. It
      asserts neither one returns `None` for a sha the function had
      already read.
    witness: tests/test_session.py::test_a_sha_the_volume_already_answered_survives_any_later_export_failure
    wrong_versions:
      - "`head_sha` is still copied from a `read_sha` local into the outer name only after both writes succeed, so a `patch.json` write failing after a successful `patch.diff` write returns `None`."
      - "The copy into `head_sha` moves earlier, but only to just before the `patch.json` write, after `patch.diff` is already written, so a failed changed-files read still returns `None`."
      - "`head_sha` is bound right after its own read, but the changed-files read is moved ahead of it, so a failed changed-files read still loses the sha it would otherwise have kept."
      - "The outer `except Exception as exc:` is changed to `return None, subjects` unconditionally, dropping whatever `head_sha` the `try` had already bound."
      - "`head_sha`'s initial value changes from `None` to the empty string, so a read that never ran at all reads as an answered sha of zero length."
      - "The `patch.diff` write and the `patch.json` write are reordered so `patch.json` is attempted first, changing which file survives a write failure without fixing what `head_sha` the `except` returns."
---

## Context

`SA-0370` is cited against `b-f582ee`'s record and the origin head
`623e5056650b5189b253f2430597fc5113919113`. `_export_from_volume`'s
`head_sha` was computed and `patch.diff` was written before `patch.json`
was built from a `changed_files` call that could still fail. That
discarded the computed sha on exactly the recovery path `SA-0369` added.
`SA-0369`'s own review, `12e8c6a6308e8e63bbf00208a908965b89e91064`, already
moved that `changed_files` call ahead of both writes
(`saffron/cell/session.py:1004-1008`). A failed read no longer orphans a
`patch.diff` with no `patch.json`. That review did not move the
*assignment* of the outer `head_sha` the same distance. The assignment
still happens on the line after both writes (`:1009`). The same class of
loss survives in a narrower window. A `patch.json` write that itself fails
once `patch.diff` is already on disk still lands in the `except` at
`:1017-1023` with `head_sha` still `None`. So, unchanged since the
finding, does the changed-files read itself.

Measured directly against `12e8c6a6`. `runtime.exec_` is stubbed dead and
the volume's `run_ephemeral` answers real git history. Monkeypatching
`Path.write_text` to raise only for a file named `patch.json` then
produces a real `patch.diff` in `task_dir`, confirmed on disk with correct
bytes. It also produces a return value of `(None, subjects)`. That is the
shape the finding describes, reached one write later than before.

**The cell path already gets this right.** `export_patch`'s own live-cell
branch binds `head_sha = worktree.head_sha(container)`
(`saffron/cell/session.py:1098`) before `task_dir.mkdir` or either write
(`:1099-1105`). Its own `except Exception as exc:` (`:1111-1113`) returns
that sha even when `worktree.changed_files`, called inline while building
`patch.json` at `:1103`, raises after `patch.diff` is already written at
`:1100`. `_export_from_volume` is the one branch that defers the
assignment past the writes.

## Problem

- **An exported patch's identity is still discardable after it is known.**
  A `patch.diff` already on disk can still be reported to the caller as
  `(None, subjects)`. That return is indistinguishable from a volume
  nothing could be read from at all. The cause is that the local variable
  holding the sha `worktree.head_sha` already answered is not the one the
  function's `except` reads.

## Out of scope

**Reordering `patch.diff` and `patch.json`'s writes.** Which file survives
a given write failure is unchanged. Only what `head_sha` comes back is
fixed.

**The cell path's own `changed_files`-after-`patch.diff` ordering
(`saffron/cell/session.py:1100-1103`).** It already preserves `head_sha`
across that failure, since `:1098` runs before `:1100`. Nothing there is
broken by this finding. Reordering its writes is a separate concern this
spec does not take up.

**Any change to `saffron/cell/worktree.py`.** `VolumeTarget`,
`commit_subjects`, `export_patch`, `head_sha` and `changed_files` are
unchanged. Only the binding of their already-returned answer, inside
`session.py`, moves.

**`tests/test_worktree.py`.** No behaviour there changes.

## Notes for the agent

**The fix.** In `_export_from_volume`
(`saffron/cell/session.py:1003-1009` at base), drop the `read_sha` local
entirely. Assign `worktree.head_sha(target)`'s answer straight to the
function's own `head_sha` the moment it returns. Do this before
`worktree.changed_files` is called, before `task_dir.mkdir`, and before
either `write_text`. Nothing else in the four lines around it changes.
`files` is still read right after, and `task_dir` is still made.
`patch.diff` is still written first. `patch.json` is still built from
`_patch_json` with the same two values. The one-line comment already above that block
(`:1003`) can be extended to say why the binding now happens first. It
must stay accurate about the write order it already describes.

**Existing test that changes.**
`test_a_volume_that_cannot_be_read_either_ends_the_export_once`'s `cell-5`
case (`tests/test_session.py`, "A volume whose file list alone cannot be
read writes neither file") asserts `head5 is None` at base. That assertion
encodes the same loss this spec fixes. The changed-files read it fails
runs after `head_sha` is already known. Once the fix lands, that case must
return the real sha instead, while still writing neither file. Update that
one assertion in place. Do not rename the test, since `census` compares
test names.

**The witness.** A real repo in `tmp_path` stands for the volume, built
with `tests/test_session.py`'s own `_volume_repo` and read under
`_pin_diff_noprefix`. Stub `runtime.exec_` dead with the existing
`_exec_dead`, and stub `runtime.create_network` /
`remove_network` / `networks_on_subnet` / `remove_container` with the
existing `_stub_export_network`. Drive two cases against the same volume.
Each gets its own `task_dir` and its own call to `session.export_patch`
with `volume=`, `image=` and `created=`:

- The changed-files read failing: stub `runtime.run_ephemeral` with the
  existing `_run_ephemeral_against(repo, [], from_dir=tmp_path,
  fail_holding="--name-only")`, so only the `git diff --name-only` call
  fails and no file was written yet. Assert the returned sha equals
  `git rev-parse HEAD` read directly against the real repo, and that no
  file landed in that case's `task_dir`.
- The `patch.json` write failing: stub `runtime.run_ephemeral` with a
  working `_run_ephemeral_against(repo, [], from_dir=tmp_path)`, with no
  `fail_holding`. Monkeypatch `pathlib.Path.write_text` to raise only when
  `self.name == "patch.json"`, delegating to the real method otherwise.
  Assert `patch.diff` exists in that case's `task_dir`, `patch.json` does
  not, and the returned sha still equals the same `git rev-parse HEAD`.

Both cases must assert that an `export_failed` teardown line is emitted,
watched through `describe`, as the existing witnesses in this file do. The
second case must also assert that no `exported` line is emitted, since the
write failed.

**Measured on a prototype built to this spec.** The diff drops the
`read_sha` local in `_export_from_volume`. It also adds one witness test,
plus a two-line change to the existing `cell-5` assertion. That measured
31 changed tokens on `size_gate` outside `tests/**`, and 297 with the
tests included, against the `bug` ceiling of 1300. `tests/test_session.py` and
`tests/test_worktree.py` both pass in full. The witness fails against the
file reverted to its `12e8c6a6` state. It also fails against each of four
hand-built wrong versions. One keeps the unmodified base ordering.
Another binds the sha right before the `patch.json` write instead of
right after the read. A third reads the changed files ahead of the sha.
A fourth makes the outer `except` return `None` unconditionally.

Commit after each coherent step. Uncommitted work dies with the cell.
